keyFindings.description: A failed first resolution of the holder ends a handover at Debug and returns nil, so reportKeptRoleDrain logs nothing and the copies wait for the sweep, or age out while the session reads keep failing. The doc's premise is false: resolveRoleHolder returns an error only for a read that failed, and a role nobody holds comes back roleHolderUnclaimed with a nil error, which already ends the handover at :552. This is round 5's lane-read finding again, on the other read.

A failed lane-head read now retries for the full 10-minute window even for a keep's handover of a role nobody holds, and never reaches the holder check. hold (:240) ignores ctx, and the window starts before it (:361, :431), so with persistent failures (an undecodable cursor, a bus refusing reads) every keep queues one goroutine on the role's guard and each ends in one Error line. Fix both findings with one rule: on a failed read, retry with backoff only while the cached claim (cfg.registry.CachedRoleHolder, as the sweep reads it) names a session; otherwise end at Debug. Treat a failed holder resolution the same way, and drop the walked branch.

holderUnresolved has one caller; the backoff pair is written three times; ended() is used at two exits and err at five, which agree only because headErr is reset on every pass. Use one retry helper and return ended() everywhere. The roleKeepDrainBackoff doc (:409-414) omits the failed head read.

The sweep now starts a handover for every claimed role with any kept copy, drained lanes included, and logs 'found a lane no handover was draining' for each, which is wrong for a drained lane. Reword it, or log it in the handover after the head read.
